app.title: Vagalume: Treino (training mode for vetting variable-star candidates)
app.summary: A person works through a shuffled set of practice cases whose answers are already known, with equal numbers of each answer. For each case they look at two diagnostic images: the light curve folded at the measured period, and a map of which pixel carries the signal. They also see the case's key numbers and a six-item checklist with the pipeline's suggestion. They choose Confirm, Doubt or Discard and are scored, with Doubt worth half a point. The right answer is then revealed with an explanation and a pointer to the panel that held the clue. For confirmed cases a second question asks whether the true period is P or 2P. Every answer is saved, and a history panel shows overall accuracy, accuracy over the last 20 answers and accuracy for each correct answer. It also gives a reviewer level, so the person can see whether they are ready to review real candidates and whether they lean towards one answer.

task.text: Train a person to vet candidate periodic signals by practising keep, doubt or drop decisions on cases with known answers, and track how accurate and how biased their decisions are.

data.text: A prepared set of practice cases. Each case is a periodic signal found in one star's light curve, with diagnostic figures, a record of the measured quantities, a known correct decision and an explanation. Each answer the person gives is saved to a history.
data.item: one star's detected periodic signal, shown as folded-light-curve and per-pixel-map images with its period, amplitude, signal strength, offset and checks in other sectors

stage.text: practising candidate vetting on known cases before reviewing real candidates

mechanism.text: A balanced, shuffled queue shows one case at a time. Its two diagnostic images sit above a set of fact cards and a rubric-style checklist that suggests an answer. A decision panel scores the choice, then reveals the answer, the explanation and the clue, and can ask a follow-up period question with the 2P panel. A collapsible guide sets good and bad example panels side by side, and a history panel adds up accuracy overall, recently and for each correct answer to give a level.

field.text: light-curve vetting of periodic variable-star candidates in time-domain astronomy

workflow.name: practise keep-or-drop decisions on items with known answers and track accuracy

steps.here: known-answer cases are loaded from the training table, cut to the same number per answer (half the extra discards taken from the higher-amplitude ones) and shuffled for each session

steps.step: learn what to look for, with good and bad examples
steps.here: a collapsible guide explains how to read folded curves and asks one question per panel. It shows a good and a bad example image from other training cases, never the one on screen

the P-folded light curve and the per-pixel signal map are shown side by side, each captioned with its question, above cards for period, amplitude, Tmag, signal offset and other sectors, and a ✅/⚠️/❌ checklist with the pipeline's suggestion

steps.step: decide keep or drop for each item, with a reason
steps.here: Confirm, Doubt or Discard is scored against the known answer (Doubt earns half a point), then the right answer, its explanation and the panel that held the clue are revealed

steps.step: answer a follow-up question about the item
steps.here: for confirmed cases with a catalogue period, the 2P-folded panel appears with a reminder figure and the question 'P or 2P?', which is scored separately and explained with the case's amplitude and period

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: Previous and Next buttons move through 'Case i of N'. Going back to a case shows the answer already given without scoring it again. At the end a total is shown, with an option to start over

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: the header shows points out of cases answered. A history expander gives accuracy overall, over the last 20 answers, for each correct answer and on the period question, and a level line (Aprendiz, Revisor or Revisor confiável) names the next threshold

distinctive: Cases are balanced by correct answer, and accuracy is also broken down by correct answer, so a bias such as confirming almost everything shows up
A middle 'doubt' answer earns half a point
After each answer the interface points to which diagnostic panel held the clue: folded curve, pixel map, other sectors or a known instrument period
A second, separately scored question asks whether the true period is the measured one or twice it (P or 2P), the classic half-period mistake with eclipsing binaries
The reviewer level is based on the last 20 answers, with accuracy thresholds and a minimum accuracy for each correct answer before the person counts as a trusted reviewer
